name: Mikhail Gorbachev

summary.text: Mikhail Gorbachev was General Secretary of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union at the time of the Chernobyl accident of 26 April 1986. This record covers only his and the Politburo's Chernobyl decisions as documented in Politburo records published by the National Security Archive and in his own public statements. The Politburo held an extraordinary session on 28 April 1986 that resolved to issue information about the accident, created an Operational Group under Nikolai Ryzhkov that first met on 29 April, and Gorbachev made his first public statement on the accident on television on 14 May 1986.

sources.title: Top Secret Chernobyl: The Nuclear Disaster through the Eyes of the Soviet Politburo, KGB, and U.S. Intelligence. Volume 1

facts.claim: At an extraordinary Politburo session on 28 April 1986 the leadership debated how to word a public statement; Andrei Gromyko argued it should not cause excessive anxiety or panic, and the session's resolution was headed 'Information about the accident at the fourth block of the Chernobyl NPS' and included preparing a press announcement.
facts.quote: Information about the accident at the fourth block of the Chernobyl NPS

sources.title: Extraordinary Session of the CC CPSU Politburo

facts.claim: Notes from Politburo member Vitaly Vorotnikov's diary of the 29 April 1986 session record that Vladimir Dolgikh's report described the situation as catastrophic, that Gorbachev criticized the nuclear industry leadership and scientists, and that the session decided to establish a standing group for communications with Chernobyl.
facts.quote: Gorbachev criticized the nuclear industry leadership and scientists, and at the end of the session Gorbachev gives sweeping instructions on removing several ministers and lower-level officials.

sources.title: CC CPSU Politburo Session (from Vitaly Vorotnikov Diary)
April 29, 1986 Politburo Session Notes [from the Diary of Vitaly Vorotnikov]

facts.claim: The Politburo Operational Group on Chernobyl, headed by Nikolai Ryzhkov, held its first meeting on 29 April 1986; its protocols were published in Russian in 1992 by Alla Yaroshinskaya and republished in English by the National Security Archive.
facts.quote: the first meeting of the Politburo group was held on April 29, 1986.

sources.title: CC CPSU Politburo Operational Group Session Protocol #1

facts.claim: A CIA National Intelligence Daily of 2 May 1986 reported that Soviet coverage of the Kiev May Day celebrations projected an appearance of normalcy, with Politburo member Shcherbytsky presiding over the festivities.
facts.quote: Soviet coverage of the Kiev May Day celebrations projected an appearance of normalcy, with Politburo member Shcherbitskiy presiding over the festivities.

sources.title: Two Articles on Chernobyl (2 May 1986 NID)

facts.claim: The Operational Group's protocol of 8 May 1986 records that the Ministry of Health approved new permissible radiation exposure standards for the population that were ten times the former standards.
facts.quote: the Health Ministry set new permissible exposure standards, surpassing the former by 10 times

facts.claim: Gorbachev's first public comment on the accident came in a television address on 14 May 1986, eighteen days after the explosion, in which he said the disaster had deeply touched the hearts of the Soviet people but that the worst was behind us.
facts.quote: Soviet leader Mikhail Gorbachev, speaking publicly about the Chernobyl nuclear accident for the first time, today said the disaster 'deeply touched the hearts of the Soviet people' but that 'the worst is behind us.' The speech was Gorbachev's first comment on the accident at Chernobyl 18 days ago.

sources.title: Soviet leader Mikhail Gorbachev, speaking publicly about the Chernobyl...

facts.claim: In the 14 May 1986 address Gorbachev said that, in view of the extraordinary and dangerous nature of what happened at Chernobyl, the Politburo had taken charge of the entire organization of the response.
facts.quote: In view of the extraordinary and dangerous nature of what happened at Chernobyl, the Politbiuro took charge of the entire organization of the work needed to ensure the speediest possible action to control the accident and limit its effects.

openQuestions: The site says the Politburo decided to hold the Kiev May Day parade. No Politburo minute or Operational Group protocol recording such a decision was found in the National Security Archive or Wilson Center results; the 28 and 29 April records deal with the information statement, the Operational Group and evacuation. A blog (Window on Eurasia) and a secondary summary say Shcherbytsky asked Gorbachev to cancel the parade and was refused; this rests on secondary accounts and was not confirmed from a primary document.

The site says the leadership 'suppressed alerts for 72 hours until Swedish Forsmark detectors alarmed'. The Politburo's information resolution is dated 28 April 1986, about two and a half days after the explosion; sources returned say the first TASS announcement that day was very brief. The Swedish detection is widely reported but no primary source for it was returned.
The site's claim that party officials 'secretly flew their children out of Kiev via Borispol Airport' was not supported by any source returned.
The site's claim that the KGB confirmed fatal radiation levels within hours was not found in the KGB documents listed by the National Security Archive in the results returned.

The Wilson Center Digital Archive holds minutes of the Kiev party city committee operative group of 7 May 1986 (restricting time on beaches and in parks); these are city-level records and were not read in full.
The entity id is typed 'unknown' in entities.json; it is a person.
